Administration

Users

Sign-ins are created automatically when a party, lawyer, or judge is saved with an email and ID number (username = email, one-time password = ID). You can also create users manually here.

Microsoft 365 & Teams

Connect Microsoft 365 for cloud sync and email, and generate the Teams app package to run inside Microsoft 365. This is admin setup — staff and judges don't need it.

Add user

For court staff, judges, and administrators. To give a party, lawyer, or representative a sign-in, add them in the Registry instead (with their email + ID) — that creates and emails their sign-in for you.

Give the one-time password to the person privately — they will be required to replace it at first sign-in.

Sign-in server

Connect a sign-in server so people can log in from any device automatically — no publishing files. When a user is created with an email, the app emails them their login details (via the server, or your Microsoft 365 mailbox). Setup instructions are in SIGNIN-SERVER.md in the download.

“Publish case data” uploads this device’s cases so judges and parties can see them on their own devices. Do this once from an admin device after setup, and any time you want to force-refresh what everyone sees.

Publish config.json next to index.html once so every device (including parties) learns the server URL and can sign in. You only re-publish if the server URL changes.

No server yet? Use a published directory instead

Without a server, publish a static roster: it contains only usernames, roles and salted hashes — no case data or plain passwords.

Place it next to index.html; re-publish whenever you add users. Microsoft 365 sync also carries the roster between court devices automatically.

All users

Generate a fresh one-time password for many users at once — sets it on the sign-in server and emails it (if a mailbox is connected). Each person is asked to set their own password at next sign-in.

Share the Excel once (paste its OneDrive/SharePoint link), then pull the latest anytime using your Microsoft sign-in — no separate Microsoft 365 setup, and it works even when a plain link is blocked.

Recognizes the Section B1 MAIN REGISTRY layout automatically (stages, parties, bench, and timeline dates are extracted), or any sheet with a header row containing “Case number”. Uses the merge/replace mode below.

Export copies all cases as JSON (for backup, or for me to read in chat). Import replaces or merges cases from JSON.

Sections of the court

All sections the court overview aggregates. Add new sections as the court grows. A section can be removed only when it has no cases.

Cases I participate in

Cases where you sit as a panel member (not presiding), grouped by section. Tap a case to open its file.

Schedule a hearing / deadline

Set a hearing date (or a deadline) on a case. It appears in Hearings & deadlines, on the case timeline, and can be reminded like any other.

New request to the court

Your request is sent to the section and stays pending until court staff review it. You'll see the status update here.

Attach a filing, document or photo (max 3 MB).

New target

Set a goal, choose how it's measured, and share it with staff and other judges. Co-owning judges can update it too.

File an application / order request

Ask the court for a stay order, procedural objection, interim order, remand, passport hold, or another order. The court will usually serve it on the other parties for an answer, then decide.

If the court will give the other parties time to answer, set the date here (can be set when serving).

Serve on the other parties

Choose who must answer this application and by when. Served parties will see it on their case and can file an answer.

View as another user

Preview the app exactly as each role sees it — navigation, which cases are visible, and what can be edited. You stay signed in as the administrator; changes made while previewing are live, so this is best for looking, not editing.

Review registry changes

These changes update the registry and are reflected across the whole app — case files, notifications, sign-ins, and every section. Please confirm.

Microsoft 365

Email ready to send

Attachments are sent only via Send now (the connected section mailbox). Mail app / Outlook Web / Copy can't carry the file automatically — attach it yourself there. Max 3 MB.

Mail app Outlook Web

Contact & notification

Anyone saved with an email + ID number automatically gets a sign-in to this app: username = email address, one-time password = ID number (they must change it at first sign-in). Sending opens a pre-drafted email in your mail app; the notification is recorded on the case timeline.
